lawyer:
Rais Uddin Ahmed, Advocate-----For the Petitioner. 
AY Masihuzzaman, Advocate-----For the Opposite Party No.1.
parties:
Bangladesh ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Abdul Aziz and others ----- Decree-holder Opposite Parties
full_judgment: 9. Mr Rais Uddin further contended that from the materials on record and the' award itself it is obvious on the face of the record that no notice either under section 14(1) of the Act ever served upon the petitioner which prevented the petitioner from availing of their valuable right given to a party to the arbitration agreement by section 33 of the Act and the non compliance with section 14(1) and (2) also renders the instant award a nullity. Mr Rais Uddin, in this connection relied on an unreported decision of this Court given in the case of Chief Engineer; Roads and Highway, Government of the People s Republic of Bangladesh vs Messrs Concord Engineering Construction i.e., FMA No, 82 of 1993 wherein this Court by delivering judgment on 4-4-1996 observed that a duty cast upon the Court to examine the legality or validity of the award before making the same a rule of the Court under section 17 of the Act even in the absence of any objection raised by a party against the award under section 33 read with section 30 or section 16 read with section 33 of the Act. He then, submits that the High Court Division judgment was appealed against in the Appellate Division and in the Appellate Division it was registered in CA No. 9 of 2001 and the Appellate Division by their judgment dated 3-8-2004 dismissed the appeal and did not find anything to interfere with the observation given by this Court on this aspect. He, therefore, relying on this decision submits that the legal position is clear that no matter whether a party to the arbitration agreement raises any objection or not as to the legality or otherwise of an award nevertheless a duty is imposed upon the Court to examine the legal aspect of the case and if it is found that the award is according of law then only it will make the award a rule of the Court. but unfortunately in the instant case the learned Court below in making the award rule of the Court lost sight of this aspect of the case and made the award a rule of the Court simply on the ground that the present did not file objection against award within specified 30 days and hence the Court made the award a rule of the Court. On this point Mr Rais Uddin, further argued that legal position is clear and there cannot be waiver or estoppels against law. In the facts and circumstances of the case Executing Court is also under legal obligation to see if the instant decree is executable or not and to see that this Court is also entitled to examine the legality or validity of the decree in question. Mr Rais Uddin submitted that no doubt this rule arises out of an order passed by the Executing Court in Executing case No.2 of 1996 at a point of time when section 47 of the Code is no more there but nevertheless in the interest of justice an Executing Court is under the legal objection to see if the decree put into execution is in fact executable or not or in other words if it stands the security of law and in the instant case a perusal of the decree would lead us to the conclusion that the arbitrator most illegally assumed jurisdiction to arbitrate the dispute and made the award beyond time without any lawful authority which renders the decree a nullity in the eye of law. Mr Rais Uddin also on the point of nullity submitted that the arbitration proceeding as well as the execution case was started against BTTB which in fact is a department of the Government and not a corporate body and with the promulgation of Ordinance 12 of 1979 on and from 27-2-1979 the Board lost its corporate existence and became a department of the Government. Thereafter, it has lost its entity to sue or be sued on its own name and in that view of the matter also instant execution case is not maintain- able and in support of his contention he relied on a decision reported in 4BLC (AD) 216. Mr Rais Uddin further submits that an objection had been filed in the execution case by the BTTB as a Government department on behalf of the Government and that the opposite party No. 1 is also pursuing their remedy against the Board and wanted to attach lands of Khatian No. 1 which is belonging to the People's Republic of Bangladesh. Therefore, in the execution case the opposite party No. 1 is pursuing its remedy against the Government of Bangladesh but Bangladesh is not a party to that arbitration agreement and the award is also not against the Government and on that ground also the proceeding of the execution case ought to have been stopped by the Court below. Mr Rais Uddin further submits that since the opposite party No.2 pursuing their remedy against the Government and/or Government Officials in their official capacity then also the decree in question is not executable as the provision of section 82 of the Code has not been followed and a cursory view of the record of the execution case clearly indicates that the executing Court did not pay any heed to the provision of section 82 of the code and the violation of which also renders the execution proceeding a nullity. Mr Rais Uddin then attacks the award on the ground that the arbitrator has no authority in law to give interest in view of the terms of the agreement but in the instant in the case it is seen that the arbitrator has given interest to the opposite party No. I for the pre-reference period, for the period under reference and for the period till the realization of the amount and therefore he contends that on this account also the award has no legs to stand upon as it is contrary to provision of law as contained in section 29 of the Act and this vital and material legal aspect of the case was also overlooked by the executing Court in proceeding with the instant execution case.
